title: NetPulse Overdrive — verified evidence ledger and Mission Control
vantage: non-Iranian lab network (Windows 11, direct HTTPS egress 83.229.87.141, AS204548)
summary: Mission Control gained an evidence-first surface (/overdrive) that reads measured artifacts, the 37-entry registry and the acceptance roadmap instead of restating them. This cycle also closed the DNS leak it had just documented: names now resolve over DNS-over-TCP through the tunnel (15/15, 80 ms), IPv6 was shown to be carried inside the tunnel, and a hard-kill recovery was measured at 3.0 s. The project still cannot demonstrate an Iranian-network result, server-issued credentials, WhiteDNS or a payment path, and the grade says so.

grade.note: Honest readiness assessment, not a code-volume score. Three weighted categories (VPS provisioning, WhiteDNS, payments) are near-zero because those subsystems do not exist in a usable form, which is 30% of the weight.

categories.name: VPN functionality and real connectivity
categories.evidence: Aether tunnel verified with data-plane traffic, differing exit AS, IPv6 through the tunnel, 20/20 staged rounds, recovery in 3.0 s; free-source path 16/270 connect, 6/7 survival at 25 min. No own infrastructure, no throughput measurement, no server-issued credentials.

categories.name: Security, privacy and access control
categories.evidence: Loopback + browser-origin session gating; dashboard regression-tested for key/subscription leakage; DNS leak closed at client level; IPv6 not leaking here. Residual: DNS-through-tunnel is opt-in per caller, one default helper still resolves locally, no independent audit.

categories.name: DPI research and censorship resilience
categories.evidence: 37 sources with limitations and confidence, layered threat model, failure taxonomy, stage-level lab baselines. Zero Iranian measurements: 0/5 Iran-ready requirements, so no censorship-resistance claim is available.

categories.name: Adaptive AI and measurable learning
categories.evidence: Real deterministic engine with approved/refused strategies, confidence, explanations and a trust anchor; refuses to rank with zero observations. No demonstrated improvement over baseline (0 observations recorded).

categories.name: VPS infrastructure and provisioning
categories.evidence: The single host 206.1.96.89 was retired 2026-11-02; no provisioning, reconciliation, backup or revocation path exists today. Earlier reconciler tests are documented but not reproducible now.

categories.name: WHITEDNS and DNS reliability
categories.evidence: Zone withdrawn with the retired host (D-01); no data plane. The new in-tunnel resolver is a real DNS reliability gain but is not the WHITEDNS product path.

categories.name: Accounting, payments and subscriptions
categories.evidence: No payment provider integrated; Telegram Stars disabled by decision and owner-gated. Subscription entitlements cannot be enforced or revoked because no host-side identity exists. Nothing here is commercially usable.

categories.name: UI/UX and Mission Control
categories.evidence: Two real dashboards on live data, six-tab evidence surface, keyboard-operable tabs, reduced-motion honoured, no synthetic values, every figure traceable to an artifact. No Persian RTL layout.

categories.name: Testing, observability, documentation and recovery
categories.evidence: 1120 API + 461 web tests passing, typecheck/lint/build clean, seven measured artifacts with timestamps, journal and decision records, recovery measured rather than asserted.

caps.connectivityNote: The "no verified tunnel" cap (≤59) does not bind because a tunnel carrying real traffic was verified; the score is below the cap on its own merits.
caps.subscriptionNote: The subscription-enforcement cap (≤69) would also not bind; entitlements genuinely cannot be enforced, which is reflected in the low payment/infra categories instead of a cap.
caps.iranNote: No Iranian-network measurement exists, so Iran-specific resilience earns no credit beyond documentation.

readiness.production: NOT READY — no server-side identity issuance, no entitlement enforcement, no monitored infrastructure.
readiness.security: PARTIAL — strong local controls and no observed leak on this host; DNS-in-tunnel is opt-in and un-audited.
readiness.commercial: NOT READY — no payment provider, no purchase-to-provision path, no revocation.

topImprovements: Route every name lookup through the tunnelled resolver by default (close the remaining opt-in leak).
Obtain a consenting Iranian vantage and run the 5-requirement protocol; without it no resilience claim exists.
Restore a provisioning path (host or per-user serverless identity) so entitlements can be issued and revoked.
Integrate one real payment provider in sandbox and prove purchase → entitlement → config end to end.
Measure throughput and soak-test recovery, not just latency and one kill cycle.
